text: Treat each Golden run as a resumable transaction with a local checkpoint after every accepted seam.
rationale: A 3am failure resumes from the last valid boundary instead of reconstructing or repeating completed work.

text: Require every stage handoff to carry a one-screen recovery envelope: failed seam, reusable evidence, next owner, next action, stop condition, and escalation boundary.
rationale: The on-call engineer gets an executable diagnosis without inventing orchestration or changing worker authorship.

text: Ship an offline replay pack that reruns literal checks and source-custody validation from captured artifacts without reopening strategy stages.
rationale: Most breakages become locally reproducible while preserving the original routing and evidence chain.

text: Quarantine malformed worker artifacts behind typed handoff boundaries so unaffected outputs remain consumable.
rationale: A bad artifact triggers one bounded repair rather than paging the whole Golden pipeline.

text: Build a failure-to-recovery map during strategy selection, with one named repair path for each stage and seam.
rationale: Recovery decisions are made before the incident, eliminating ad hoc 3am diagnosis.

text: Make acceptance emit a release-neutral delivery receipt containing implementation evidence, required-test results, unresolved defects, and the explicit release-authority handoff.
rationale: A broken delivery is separated from a release decision, so on-call can close the engineering incident without assuming release authority.
